newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sentences two to death for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sentences two to death for fraud.

text.p: Vietnam sentenced two people to death on Tuesday and punished others with prison terms of up to life in a major show trial for the communist government's determination to crack down on graft.

A court official in Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) said Pham Minh Tong and Nguyen Ngoc Tan had been found guilty of fraudulent appropriation of citizens' property and would be executed by firing squad.
One defendant was sentenced to life in jail and two others were handed terms of 20 years and six years each. Two people received suspended terms and one person was found innocent.
"The sentencing is intended both as a punishment, and as a warning against any future cases," said the official, who declined to be identified. "It has caused very serious consequences."
The case, which ran for almost a week, was reported on at length in the state-controlled media, where it was billed as the country's biggest fraud trial.

Together, the defendants were charged with duping the state out of more than $12 million in cash and gold through a racket involving a fertiliser transaction -- an important commodity in Vietnam's rural-based economy.
While the trial has attracted considerable media attention the shockwaves for Vietnam go wider.
Corruption and economic crime emerged as a major issue after a Communist Party Congress held last June, adding new political overtones to an old problem.

Conservatives argue that graft has worsened with economic reforms introduced in the late 1980s. Others say it is a reflection of more fundamental problems arising, in part, from an unwieldy government bureaucracy.
Eighteen people were originally implicated in Tuesday's case, including a number of state officials and a leading suspect who fled to Cambodia in 1994.
A trial with even wider-reaching implications is set to begin later this week.
On Thursday a southern court will hear the opening arguements in a corruption case involving Ho Chi Minh City firm Tamexco -- a trading firm affiliated to the ruling Communist Party.

Investigations into the affair have uncovered a trail of graft involving several former officials of the country's largest state-owned commercial bank and running uncomfortably close to some of the nation's most powerful people.
Foreign journalists have been refused permission to attend.
